situation: A friend quotes a shocking statistic that you doubt.
say: This is fake news, bro. Where did you even get this?
better: That number surprises me. Where is it from? I'd like to check it.
also: Can you share the source? I've seen quite different figures.
weak: Totally wrong. Stop spreading WhatsApp forwards.
Haha ok, whatever you say.
why: Asks for evidence without calling the person a liar.

situation: Mid-argument, you realise the other person has made a good point.
say: Ya ya, ok fine, but still...
better: Fair point. I hadn't thought of that, and it changes my view a bit.
also: You're right about that part. Where I still disagree is the cost.
weak: Ok whatever, you win.
Fine, but that doesn't matter.
why: Conceding openly makes you more believable, not weaker.

situation: Someone keeps interrupting you before you can finish.
say: Let me speak na! You're not letting me talk at all!
better: Let me finish this point, and then I'll hear you out fully.
also: Hold on, I'm almost done. Then it's all yours.
weak: Can you please shut up for one minute?
Arre, you always do this, yaar.
why: Firm and fair: you claim your turn and promise them theirs.

situation: An argument at a family dinner is getting heated.
say: Chalo, leave it. You'll never understand anyway.
better: We're both getting heated. Let's pause this and talk about it later.
also: I don't want this to spoil dinner. Can we agree to disagree for now?
weak: Forget it, there's no point talking to you.
Fine, you're right, happy now?
why: Ends the fight without a parting insult.

situation: Someone attacks you personally instead of answering your point.
say: Look who's talking! You also did the same thing.
better: Let's keep this about the idea, not about me. What's wrong with the argument itself?
also: Even if that's true about me, it doesn't answer my point.
weak: At least I'm not as bad as you.
Very mature, very mature.
why: Pulls the debate back to the argument and away from people.

situation: You don't understand what the other person is arguing.
say: What are you even saying? It makes no sense.
better: I'm not sure I follow. Can you give me an example?
also: So are you saying that rents will fall? Tell me if I've got it wrong.
weak: You're confusing everyone, including yourself.
Ok, whatever, next point.
why: Understand first, then disagree.

situation: On a college panel, you want to disagree with a senior speaker.
say: With due respect sir, I humbly beg to differ completely.
better: I see it differently, and here's why.
also: I partly agree, but I think the data points the other way.
weak: Sorry sir, but you are totally wrong.
No offence, but that's very old-school thinking.
why: Plain disagreement with a reason sounds more confident than ritual politeness.

situation: A friend says a habit is safe because his uncle did it and lived to ninety.
say: Your uncle is just lucky, bro. That proves nothing.
better: One person's story is interesting, but it doesn't tell us what happens to most people.
also: Is there a bigger study on this? One case can mislead.
weak: Your uncle is an exception, so you're wrong.
Ok, then everyone should start doing it, na?
why: Separates a single story from the bigger evidence, politely.

situation: Mid-argument, you find out one of your facts was wrong.
say: Ok, maybe, maybe. Anyway, the main point is...
better: I was wrong about that, thanks for correcting me. Let me see if my main point still holds.
also: You're right, I mixed up the numbers. Let me rethink.
weak: That's just a small detail, it doesn't matter.
Google can also be wrong, you know.
why: Owning a mistake quickly protects your credibility.

situation: Someone backs their claim by saying 'everyone knows this'.
say: Who is this 'everyone'? Name them.
better: I'm not sure everyone agrees. What makes you say that?
also: Has that actually been shown, or is it more of a common feeling?
weak: Everyone knows nothing, ok?
That's such a dumb way to argue.
why: Questions the claim, not the person.

situation: An uncle posts a false forward in the family WhatsApp group.
say: Uncle, please don't forward such fake things.
better: Uncle, I checked this one and it seems to be false. Here's the fact-check.
also: I found a fact-check on this. Worth a look before we share it further.
weak: Uncle, this is why WhatsApp university is famous.
Seriously? Who believes this nonsense?
why: Shows the evidence and lets the other person save face.

situation: Before disagreeing, you want to show you understood your colleague's view.
say: I understood, I understood. But...
better: So your point is that the cost is too high. Fair. My worry is a different one.
also: Let me check I've got you: you think speed matters more than quality?
weak: Yes yes, I know what you mean, but no.
Ok, noted. Anyway...
why: Summing up their view proves you listened and calms things down.

situation: Someone asks you to back up something you said casually.
say: I read it somewhere, I don't remember. Just trust me.
better: Good question. I'm not sure of the source. Let me check and come back to you.
also: I may be wrong on that. I'll find the source before I repeat it.
weak: It's common sense, why do you need proof?
Google it yourself, na.
why: Be honest about what you don't know.

situation: A debate with a friend keeps going in circles.
say: Ok, same thing again and again. I'm done.
better: I think we've both made our points. Shall we see where we actually agree?
also: We're repeating ourselves. Maybe we need more facts before we decide.
weak: You're not listening, so I'm stopping.
Fine, believe what you want.
why: Moves from fighting to finding common ground.

situation: You criticise something, and someone replies, 'What about the others? They did it too.'
say: Why are you bringing that up? We are talking about this.
better: That may be wrong too, and we can discuss it. But it doesn't make this one right.
also: Both can be bad at the same time. Can we finish this one first?
weak: Classic whataboutism, you're just dodging.
Oh, so now you'll defend them?
why: Accepts the other point without letting it replace yours.

situation: In a meeting, someone wins the point by saying 'lots of customers are complaining'.
say: Lots means how many? Don't exaggerate.
better: Roughly how many complaints are we talking about? That will help us decide.
also: Do we have the actual numbers? I'd like to see the scale.
weak: I don't believe you, show me proof right now.
Everybody says 'lots' when they have no data.
why: Asks for a number without accusing anyone of exaggerating.

situation: In a college debate, your opponent claims one trend caused another because they rose together.
say: This is a very illogical point, honestly.
better: These two rose together, but that alone doesn't show one caused the other. What else could explain it?
also: Is there evidence of cause here, or only that they happened together?
weak: My opponent clearly doesn't understand basic logic.
This is just coincidence. Next point.
why: Names the exact flaw instead of just calling it illogical.

situation: After a long talk, you still disagree with a close friend.
say: Ok, you think your way, I'll think mine. Bye.
better: We see this differently, and that's fine. Thanks for actually talking it through.
also: I still disagree, but I understand your side better now.
weak: Ok, let's just never talk about this again.
You'll realise one day that I was right.
why: Ends warmly; the friendship matters more than winning.

situation: A relative starts shouting during an argument about your career choice.
say: Why are you shouting? I'm not deaf!
better: I want to hear you, but it's hard when we're shouting. Can we talk calmly?
also: Let's both lower our voices. I'll listen properly.
weak: If you shout, I'll shout louder.
Ok, do whatever you want, I'm leaving.
why: Names the problem and invites calm without matching their anger.

situation: A colleague criticises your plan, and half of the criticism is right.
say: No no, the plan is fine. You're overthinking.
better: You're right about the timeline, I'll fix that. On the budget, I still think it works.
also: Good catch on the timeline. On the budget, I see it differently.
weak: Ok, everything you said is right, I'll redo it all.
You only find problems in my work.
why: Accept what's true and defend what isn't; both make you credible.

situation: In an argument, someone dismisses you with 'You're just being emotional.'
say: I'm not emotional! You're the one being emotional!
better: I do feel strongly about this. That doesn't make my point wrong. Here's my reason.
also: Yes, it matters to me. Can we look at the reasons anyway?
weak: How dare you call me emotional?
Fine, I'll stop talking then.
why: Admit the feeling, then return to the reason.

situation: Friends want you to pick a side in a debate you know little about.
say: I don't know yaar, both are same only.
better: I don't know enough to take a side yet. What's the strongest point on each side?
also: Honestly, I'm undecided. Convince me.
weak: Whatever you say, I'm with you.
Both sides are stupid, frankly.
why: Being honestly unsure beats faking a view.

situation: Someone twists your words into something you never said.
say: You always twist my words. This is your habit.
better: That's not quite what I said. I meant we need more time, not that the idea is bad.
also: Let me be clearer: I said we should wait, not that we should drop it.
weak: You're lying, I never said that.
Ok, believe whatever you heard.
why: Correct the record calmly and restate your real point.

situation: Your manager says remote work kills productivity and asks if you agree.
say: Sir, actually it's the opposite. Everyone works more from home.
better: I've seen it go both ways. Do we have data from our own team? That would settle it.
also: Could we look at our own numbers before we decide?
weak: Sorry sir, but that's a very outdated way of thinking.
Yes sir, you are right, as always.
why: Moves the debate from opinion to evidence, respectfully.

situation: You lose a debate competition and walk up to the winner.
say: Congrats, but honestly the judges were biased.
better: Well argued. Your point on costs really landed. Congratulations.
also: You deserved it. I'd love to know how you prepared.
weak: Congrats, you got lucky with the topic.
Ok, congrats, whatever.
why: Losing gracefully earns respect; praise something specific.
